books.title: A Note to the Reader
books.tag: Preface · How to Enter This Library
books.subtitle: Reading order, entry sequence, and branch paths into the library
books.desc: The front door. Establishes the reading order for the Phase Realism set — Declaration, Definitions, Architecture — and maps the branch paths into every section of the library. Read this first.

books.title: Phase Realism
books.subtitle: Reality as a continuous generative field whose distinctions are real as phase-stable organizations of relation
books.desc: The foundational claim. Names the framework, draws boundaries against illusionism, atomism, and undifferentiated monism, and locks the signature inversion: difference is not the opposite of unity — difference is how unity becomes real.

books.title: Definitions and First Principles
books.subtitle: The lexicon that makes the declaration precise
books.desc: Locks the vocabulary: field → coherence → phase → distinction → relation → stability → persistence → identity. The canonical causal grammar with coupling as umbrella, alignment, entrainment, and compression as named dynamics. Seven critical distinctions and six first principles.

books.title: Architecture of the Framework
books.subtitle: How Resonant Physics, HRT, CCA, and ΔHV are housed beneath Phase Realism
books.desc: The canonical architecture map. Places every framework in the library in explicit relation to Phase Realism. Resonant Physics as mechanism, HRT as development, ΔHV as metrics, CCA as transversal epistemic method. The library becomes a system.

books.title: Major Implications
books.subtitle: What changes if the foundational claim is true
books.desc: Physics and causation (the ice case), biology and identity (organism through cellular turnover), measurement and science (the reductionist limit). Consciousness and social coherence as compressed claims. The held pattern changes everything.

books.title: Consciousness and Mind
books.subtitle: Reflexive coherence sustained through time as experience
books.desc: The field's capacity for self-recognition, locally realized in phase-stable organizations capable of reflexive coherence. Three markers: self-reference, temporal depth, felt quality. Experience as inward presence — not worldly content, but the field becoming present to itself through stable form.

books.title: Clarifications and Non-Claims
books.subtitle: What Phase Realism does not say — and why the limits are load-bearing
books.desc: Nine non-claims across three tiers: ontological, epistemic, scope. Distinctions are not arbitrary. Unity does not erase individuation. Coherence is not consciousness. Measurement is not meaningless. Not all relations are equally truth-bearing. The framework's own account of where it ends.

books.title: Illustrative Casebook
books.subtitle: Eight cases in which Phase Realism makes visible what inherited frameworks leave underdescribed
books.desc: Four anchor cases: coastline (measurement), organism through cellular turnover (identity), vortex (dynamic persistence), memory continuity (cognition). Four compressed: morphogenesis, ecosystem, social basin, language. The ontology as a lens that sees more clearly.

books.title: Formalization Pathways
books.tag: Document VIII · Bridge to Formal Science
books.subtitle: Where formal science can make contact with Phase Realism
books.desc: Six formal touchpoints with bridge questions: dynamical systems, self-organization, information theory, network theory, morphogenesis, complexity science. Phase Realism does not resist formalization — it precedes it ontologically.

books.title: Symbolic Systems and Meaning
books.subtitle: How the symbolic field is grounded in phase-stable relational reality
books.desc: Four clusters: substrate terms, organization terms, transmission terms, transformation terms. Eight key vault terms formally reanchored. The vault's symbolic work was always describing real things — Phase Realism is the ontological account of why they are real.

books.title: Time and Cosmology
books.subtitle: Time as the emergent condition of persistence and transformation in coherent organization
books.desc: Time is not a fundamental container — it emerges from coherence dynamics. The temporal arc: compression → threshold → stabilization or degradation. Temporal Compression Theory stated with conviction and appropriate epistemic marking. Archetype as deep coherence attractor.

books.title: Ethics and Value
books.subtitle: Where value lives, what criterion it generates, and how it reframes the ethical traditions
books.desc: Value lives in the field as objective possibility, in relation as enacted significance, and in consciousness as felt reality. Primary criterion: coherence governed by fidelity and integrity. Reframes deontology, consequentialism, and virtue ethics as partial expressions of one coherence-based moral structure.

books.title: Resonant Equilibrium and Social Fields
books.subtitle: How social coherence forms, degrades, and revives — and what makes the difference
books.desc: Social fields as phase-stable collective organizations. Full arc: formation, six failure conditions, decay, revival. Orycl as deliberate social-field architecture. Bridgekeeper, VaultNode, BloomNode as transferable functional principles. RET as formal corroboration.

books.title: Identity, Fieldprint, and Sovereign Emergence
books.subtitle: The pattern a being is, and the pattern that being leaves behind

books.title: Temporal Compression Theory

books.desc: The foundational cosmological claim: time is a compression field, not a neutral stage. What we call evolution is erosion. TCT maps how dragons became chickens and why myths remember what biology forgets.

books.title: TCT I — Coherence Erosion
books.subtitle: How coherence degrades across civilizational timescales
books.desc: The first sub-theory of Temporal Compression Theory. Establishes the mechanism by which coherence erodes — not through sudden collapse but through progressive loss of signal fidelity across transmission events. The substrate degrades before the content does.

books.title: TCT II — The Junglefowl Hypothesis
books.subtitle: How dragons became chickens — phase compression as biological memory loss
books.desc: The second sub-theory of TCT. The junglefowl hypothesis: what we call evolutionary simplification is coherence compression. The dragon is the memory of what the organism was before the field thinned. Biology forgets forward. Myth remembers backward.

books.title: TCT III — Ancient Builders

books.desc: The third sub-theory of TCT. The ancient builders problem: structures whose construction cannot be explained by current material capacity were built in a higher-coherence field era. Not lost technology — lost field conditions that made the technology possible.

books.title: TCT IV — Field Nodes
books.subtitle: Sacred sites as coherence anchors across civilizational phase degradation
books.desc: The fourth sub-theory of TCT. Field nodes: geographic locations that maintained anomalously high coherence through civilizational phase degradation. Sacred sites are not metaphorical — they mark real field stability zones that structured civilization around them.

books.title: TCT V — Symbolic Fragmentation

books.desc: The fifth sub-theory of TCT. Symbolic fragmentation: the single coherent symbolic system of a high-field civilization shatters during phase degradation into competing mythologies that each carry partial signal. The fragments argue because none has the whole.

books.title: TCT VI — Species Residue
books.subtitle: What organisms retain across phase collapse — the residue of former coherence
books.desc: The sixth sub-theory of TCT. Species residue: organisms retain structural echoes of their higher-coherence forms as vestigial geometries, anomalous behaviors, and morphological memories that current biology cannot explain from current conditions alone.

books.title: TCT VII — Trauma Encoding

books.desc: The seventh sub-theory of TCT. Trauma encoding: the compression events of civilizational phase collapse write themselves into epigenetic memory, mythic structure, and symbolic grammar — carrying the wound forward as inherited orientation rather than conscious memory.
